McLaren.summary: McLaren has tweaked the rear wing’s side panels to smooth the airflow and fitted a brand‑new wing set‑up that cuts drag for this particular circuit. The result should be a tighter, more stable rear end that lets the car hug corners better while still staying fast on the straights. In short, the car will feel more planted and quicker, giving the drivers a tangible edge this weekend.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes have tweaked the rear wing to run a flatter angle on the upper panels, shaving off drag and giving the car a little extra straight‑line speed on this circuit’s long straights. The small rear “drum” winglets have been repositioned and made a touch wider to sharpen rear‑end stability through the fast corners. Finally, the top edge of the front‑wing endplates is now more pronounced, helping clean up the airflow into the front of the car for better grip off the start‑line and into the first bends.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has tweaked the rear‑wing’s little vertical elements, giving them a new shape that smooths out airflow over the car. The change should boost down‑force consistency, especially in the fast, flowing corners, helping the team stick closer to the racing line and defend better this weekend.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams have tweaked three key aero pieces for the weekend: a new rear‑brake‑duct winglet to clean up the airflow and cut drag, a subtle reshaping of the floor’s outer edge to suit the circuit’s characteristics, and a revised floor profile that widens the central diffuser to boost down‑force. In plain terms, these changes should give the car a steadier rear end and a bit more grip through the corners without sacrificing straight‑line speed, helping Williams be more competitive on this track.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls has tweaked the car’s aerodynamics – reshaping the engine cover, side‑pods and roll‑hoop inlet – to smooth the airflow over the front and rear, which should give a cleaner, more stable ride on the straights and through fast corners. A new brake‑drum layout improves front‑end grip off the brakes, while a fresh upper rear‑wing piece adds a bit more bite at the back, helping the car stay glued to the track in high‑speed sections. Together these tweaks aim to shave off lap‑time and give the drivers a more predictable, faster package for the weekend.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has reshaped the front wing, adding a small “beam” element to shave off drag while tweaking the wing’s corners and end‑plates to push more air down onto the tires where it counts most. The result is a car that should feel stickier into the fast bends and a touch quicker on the straights, giving the drivers a better‑balanced package for qualifying and the race this weekend.

Audi F1 Team.summary: Audi’s weekend update tweaks two aero pieces to match the track’s character. The rear‑wing’s upper element has been reshaped to give a tighter drag range, letting the car stay stable on the straights while still grabbing enough down‑force through the corners. At the rear, a new side‑wall winglet on the diffuser helps keep the car glued to the tarmac, especially in high‑speed sections, so drivers can push harder without losing confidence.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has tweaked the top of the car by reshaping the halo fairing and adding a small winglet. The new shape smooths the airflow over the cockpit, giving a modest bump in down‑force and better cooling for the driver. In short, it should help the car stick to the track a little more reliably during this weekend’s sprint.

Cadillac.summary: Cadillac has tweaked the back‑edge of its front wing – reshaping the footplates and adding a new horizontal vane – to smooth the airflow over the car. The result is a cleaner, more stable front end that should give better grip out of corners and help the team keep the car glued to the track this weekend. In short, the car will feel more planted, letting drivers push harder through the fast turns.
